items.headline: Singapore rolls out haze subsidies and N95 masks as air stays unhealthy
items.summary: From 12 October eligible Singaporeans can get subsidised treatment for haze-related conditions at all polyclinics and participating GP clinics under a new Haze Subsidy Scheme, as the reconvened Haze Task Force prepared to distribute N95 masks and warned the 24-hour PSI could pass 200.

items.headline: Two men arrested over trespassing at the Singapore Grand Prix
items.summary: Police arrested two men over trespassing at the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix after one, aged 39, allegedly used an invalid ticket and later reached a restricted staff-and-artiste area.

items.headline: Singapore police flag scams as a woman, 63, loses S$4,000 to an impersonator
items.summary: A 63-year-old Singaporean woman lost about S$4,000 in a scam, prompting the Bishan Neighbourhood Police Centre to post an advisory on 9 October about fraudsters impersonating active-ageing-centre staff.

items.headline: Italian man jailed eight years and caning for trafficking a Singaporean woman to Dubai
items.summary: A 32-year-old Italian man was sentenced in Singapore on 7 October to eight years in jail and caning for trafficking a Singaporean woman to Dubai and forcing her into sex work.

items.headline: India frees detained protesters after the Supreme Court calls the crackdown illegal
items.summary: India released thousands of detained protesters, including three Cockroach Janta Party leaders freed on Sunday, after the Supreme Court called the detentions illegal; Rahul Gandhi was briefly held and the movement vowed to keep demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

items.headline: RBI opens a special oil-dollar window to defend the rupee near record lows
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India let state-run oil companies buy dollars through a special window from Monday and tightened hedging rules to ease pressure on the rupee, which is hovering near record lows.

items.headline: Rupee hits record lows after the RBI's surprise rate hike and a weak monsoon
items.summary: The rupee slid to around record lows and Indian equities fell after the RBI raised interest rates and signalled more tightening, while the weakest monsoon in over a decade added to food-price and import-cost pressures.

items.headline: Burnham vows to release details of his Manchester City meetings
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would publish details of his meetings with senior Manchester City figures after criticism of his remarks on the club's guilty verdict for breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

items.headline: UK Greens leader seeks a rule change after the party declared Zionism racism
items.summary: Green Party leader Zack Polanski said he would seek to change party rules after a conference motion classified Zionism as a form of racism, a decision that has drawn cross-party criticism.

items.headline: Trump announces a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire as Zelensky says Moscow keeps striking
items.summary: Trump said on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire halting strikes on each other's power infrastructure; Zelensky said Ukraine backed it but that Russia kept hitting facilities in Kyiv and Kharkiv, and offered to stop attacks on Russian refineries if Moscow complied.

items.headline: Hurricane Simon skirts Mexico's Pacific coast after flooding Manzanillo
items.summary: Hurricane Simon tracked just off Mexico's Pacific coast on Sunday and was expected to stay offshore into Monday after flooding homes in Manzanillo; Mexico's Navy deployed more than 4,600 personnel and authorities urged residents to shelter.

items.headline: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall on the US Gulf Coast before weakening
items.summary: Hurricane Isaias, the first hurricane of the Atlantic season to strike the United States, made landfall on the Gulf Coast before weakening, after forming in the Gulf earlier in the week amid warnings it could disrupt US oil refining.

items.headline: UAE says a Flydubai co-pilot plotted a 9/11-style attack on Israel
items.summary: UAE prosecutors said a Flydubai co-pilot had planned a premeditated terrorist attack inspired by 9/11, aiming to crash a Tel Aviv-bound jet into the terminal at Ben Gurion Airport; the 30 September flight carrying 174 people was saved by the crew and landed in Saudi Arabia.

items.headline: OpenAI's revenue is reportedly $20 billion below projections as its IPO slips to 2027
items.summary: OpenAI's annualised revenue is running about $20 billion below an earlier $70 billion projection, according to a report, with the company said to have pushed any public listing to early 2027.

items.headline: AI leaderboard LMArena raises $200 million at a $3.1 billion valuation
items.summary: LMArena, which runs the popular crowd-sourced AI model leaderboard, raised a $200 million Series B led by Lightspeed and Khosla Ventures, nearly doubling its valuation to about $3.1 billion in 10 months.

items.headline: Aurora and Kodiak win a US exemption to run driverless trucks
items.summary: US regulators granted Aurora and Kodiak a federal exemption clearing a regulatory roadblock for self-driving trucks, in the same week Waymo took its first debt financing, a $5 billion raise.

items.headline: Vesta raises $30 million to bring AI agents to mortgage lenders
items.summary: Vesta raised $30 million, led by Conversion Capital, to deploy teams of AI agents at mortgage lenders, part of a wave of startups selling automation to financial-services firms.

items.headline: Big US banks open a bumper third-quarter earnings season
items.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Wells Fargo are all due to report this week, kicking off a third-quarter US earnings season that analysts expect to show strong year-on-year profit growth.

items.headline: Oil climbs on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a US-Russia diesel deal
items.summary: Oil prices rose, with Brent crude around $105 a barrel, as markets weighed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a US-brokered arrangement to keep Russian diesel flowing to global markets.

items.headline: Nvidia is in talks to back AI startup Reflection, the FT reports
items.summary: Nvidia is in early talks to invest in or provide computing power to Reflection AI, the Financial Times reported, the latest sign of the chipmaker funnelling capital into the AI startups that buy its chips.

items.headline: Verstappen wins the Singapore Grand Prix for his first Marina Bay victory
items.summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time, on his 250th race start, finishing 7.3 seconds clear of Charles Leclerc with Kimi Antonelli third, a podium that extended Antonelli's championship lead; Norris and Piastri were fourth and fifth.

items.headline: Hamilton apologises over a Ferrari strategy call at the Singapore Grand Prix
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton apologised over a Ferrari strategy call at the Singapore Grand Prix, where the team finished second through Charles Leclerc but could not challenge winner Max Verstappen.

items.headline: Zverev reaches the Shanghai Masters last 16 for his 60th win of 2026
items.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Quentin Halys 6-4, 6-7 (8), 6-3 to reach the Shanghai Masters round of 16 and, by the ATP's count, record his 60th match win of 2026; he next faces Alexander Bublik.

items.headline: India beat West Indies by 14 runs to lead the T20I series 2-1
items.summary: India beat West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I at Indore, posting 223 and restricting the tourists to 209 for 7; Abhishek Sharma made 69 and Arshdeep Singh took 3 for 44 as India moved 2-1 up in the five-match series.

items.headline: Astronomers detect the oldest and most distant fast radio burst yet
items.summary: Astronomers using South Africa's MeerKAT array reported the most distant fast radio burst found to date, a millisecond flash from a galaxy at redshift 2.1, about 3 billion years after the Big Bang, that could help map matter between galaxies. Published in Science.

items.headline: NASA's SPHEREx telescope captures a menagerie of brown dwarfs
items.summary: NASA said its SPHEREx telescope, which is mapping the whole sky in infrared, had imaged a varied population of brown dwarfs, objects too big to be planets but too small to sustain the hydrogen fusion that powers stars.

items.headline: A Jurassic fossil reveals a platypus-like swimming mammal relative
items.summary: Researchers described Megacauda sungei, a roughly 165-million-year-old mammal relative from Inner Mongolia with a flattened tail and platypus-like, water-foraging lifestyle; its throat anatomy suggests suckling and swallowing evolved in early mammal ancestors. Published in Nature.

items.headline: Startup unveils the first microbe designed for Mars, but experts are skeptical
items.summary: The nonprofit Pioneer Labs said it had engineered the first microbe for Mars, sPL.001, designed to turn Martian dirt, water and carbon dioxide into bioplastic in a bioreactor; outside scientists called it a manufacturing tool rather than a step toward terraforming.

fun_fact.headline: The word OK began as an 1839 joke spelling of 'oll korrect'
fun_fact.body: The word OK, probably the most spoken word on Earth, began as a joke. It first appeared in print in The Boston Morning Post on 23 March 1839 as a deliberately misspelled abbreviation of 'oll korrect' (all correct). Its survival was cemented a year later by Martin Van Buren's 1840 re-election campaign, which nicknamed him 'Old Kinderhook' and set up 'OK Clubs'.

puzzle.title: Four Anglers, Three Fish
puzzle.body: Two fathers and two sons spend the afternoon fishing. Each of them catches exactly one fish and takes it home, yet the family brings home only three fish. None was lost, thrown back, or eaten. How can that be?
puzzle.approach: Count the people, not the roles - one person can fill more than one.
puzzle.answer: There were only three people fishing: a grandfather, his son, and his grandson. The grandfather and his son are the 'two fathers'; the son and the grandson are the 'two sons'. The middle man counts as both, so three people fill all four roles and three fish come home.

word_puzzle.title: Deep End
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter O (required in every word). Outer letters: D, L, P, H, I, N. Make words of four or more letters using only these seven letters (letters may repeat); every word must contain O. One word, the pangram, uses all seven.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word uses the centre letter O and only the seven given letters; find the seven-letter pangram.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: DOLPHIN. Other valid words: HOLD, IDOL, LION, LOIN, POLO, POND, POOL, LOON, NOON, HOOD, HOOP, PLOD, HIPPO.
